newsitem.title: UK: WORLD BONDS-Gilts to gain in long run under Labour.
newsitem.headline: WORLD BONDS-Gilts to gain in long run under Labour.

text.p: A landslide victory for Britain's opposition Labour party ultimately will benefit the gilt market, despite the greater than forecast extent of Labour's gains, analysts said on Friday.

"Our forecast is for the gilt/Bund spread to narrow to 120 basis points by December," said Huw Roberts, bond strategist at NatWest Markets in London. "We made that forecast before the election and it has not changed since."
All the opinion polls favoured Labour to win the election and end 18 years of Conservative rule.
But the size of Labour's majority defied expectations.
By 0529 GMT, Labour had won 417 seats to Conservative's 160 and third party Liberal Democrat's 40, with results from the final 31 seats still to come in.
"Potentially this is very good news for gilts," said Guy Chalkley, fund manager at Robert Fleming Investment Management.
"Labour has such a strong majority that it does not have to woo the left of the party. It can press ahead with the policy initiatives of the campaign."
Gilts dipped on Friday in an initial reaction to a huge victory for a left-wing party.
